claims.head: Fresh legs against tired ones
claims.body: It’s the Senators’ second game in two nights. Teams on the back end of those usually spend more time defending, so we think the Blues get more of the play than usual.
claims.call: The Blues get a bigger share of the 5-on-5 chances than they usually do.
claims.nums: Ottawa played yesterday · St. Louis had 2 days off · St. Louis’s usual share of 5-on-5 expected goals: 51.8%
claims.gist: The Senators played last night; the Blues are rested.

check.measure: share of 5-on-5 expected goals, adjusted for score and venue
check.rule: held if the rested team's share of 5-on-5 expected goals is at or above its usual share; otherwise didn't happen

claims.head: Bring a pillow
claims.call: The game’s pace score is below 96, slower than either team’s usual.
claims.see: Fewer than 64 shots between them at 5-on-5, on goal or wide, which usually means 54 or fewer shots on goal on the scoreboard.
claims.body: St. Louis plays some of the league’s slowest games, and so does Ottawa. We think this one is even quieter than either team’s usual.
claims.nums: Pace score (100 is league average): St. Louis 27th (96), Ottawa 28th (96)

claims.head: Active D against forward-led
claims.body: On shots from defensemen, St. Louis is near the top of the league, but Ottawa is near the bottom. Watch the Blues’ defensemen jump into the play.

notes.text: L. Mailloux is out long term and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman. A. Jiříček has taken his spot beside P. Broberg.
A. Zub is on the injured non-roster list (knee injury) and has not played this season. He is a top-four defenseman.
J. Sanderson is out (lower-body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
W. Eklund is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games.
J. Spence has started killing penalties: on the ice for 40% of the team’s shorthanded time in 6 games, up from 4% last season.

OTT.head: Too close to call
OTT.body: Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Sanderson, but they have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. For Ottawa, the difference could be a penalty kill that holds up.

STL.head: A genuine toss-up
STL.body: Ottawa is on the second night of a back-to-back and will be without Sanderson, but they have been out-chancing opponents lately and have home-ice advantage. For St. Louis, the difference could be keeping shots to a minimum.

story.head: Fresh legs against tired ones
paras: The Senators have won three straight. The Blues are 2-2-1.
Both teams play slow, low-event hockey. The Blues’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Senators’ not so much.
